questions.question: The mean of the following distribution is 50. Find the value of 'a' and hence the frequencies of 30 and 70: x: 10, 30, 50, 70, 90; f: 17, (5a+3), 32, (7a-11), 19.
A hospital tracks blood sugar levels of 25 patients: 87, 71, 77, 85, 73, 81, 69, 54, 78, 78, 83, 76, 70, 68, 81, 67, 65, 68, 85, 77, 85, 85, 80, 73, 75. Find the Mean, Median, and Mode.

Data for Ages: 20-24, 25-29, 30-34, 35-39, 40-44, 45-49, 50-54 with frequencies 10, 28, 32, 48, 50, 35, 12. Convert these to exclusive class intervals and explain why this is necessary for drawing a histogram.
solutionSteps: Subtract 0.5 from lower limits and add 0.5 to upper limits.
This is necessary so there are no gaps between rectangles in the histogram, accurately representing continuous data.

questions.question: The marks of 80 students are: 10-20 (6), 20-30 (17), 30-50 (15), 50-70 (16), 70-100 (26). Construct a table showing the adjusted frequencies ready for a histogram. Use min width 10.
Explain how to construct a frequency polygon using both (a) a histogram as a base, and (b) by directly using class marks. Use an example interval 10-20 with frequency 5.
solutionSteps: With Histogram: Draw rectangle for 10-20 (height 5). Mark mid-point of top edge (15, 5). Join such points.
With Class Marks: Calculate mark = (10+20)/2 = 15. Plot point (15, 5). Join such points.
In both cases, complete the polygon by joining to x-axis at mid-points of adjacent intervals with zero frequency.
